name: Kohlering-Technik Pirkheim GmbH
summary: Kohlering-Technik is a family-owned seal maker (140 staff, ~35 M EUR turnover, founded 1972) with stable finances. It is currently allocating standard mechanical seals based on last year's call-offs, and its delivery performance is slipping: OTD fell from 80.4 % to 75.5 % against a 95 % contract target, and ppm is rising. It runs a formal price policy: no discounts on standard items, only multi-year volume agreements change prices, and any move above 2 % goes to a pricing committee that meets every two weeks.

situation.decision_maker: Key account manager up to 2 % price change. Above that, the pricing committee, which meets every two weeks.

negotiation_pattern: It asks for moderate annual increases (mean 3.18 %) and settles far lower (mean 0.65 %). When it asks below about 4 %, it usually ends at 0 %. When it asks about 4.7–4.8 %, it gets roughly 2 % (2.1 % and 1.8 %). It never settled above 2.1 %, which matches its 2 % approval threshold. It has not yet sent a 2027 increase notice in the dossier. Its stated line is no discounts on standard items unless there is a multi-year volume deal.
wants: Multi-year volume security and reliable forecasts, the only stated lever for price changes
Predictable call-offs that fit its allocation logic
On-time payment from us (we pay late 87 % of the time)
Annual price increases of 2 % or less, which avoids the committee
protects: unit_price on standard items (no-discount policy, committee above 2 %)
Allocation volumes beyond last year's call-offs

trades.give: contract_months up (extend the framework beyond 2027-06-30 to a multi-year term)
trades.get: unit_price frozen for 2027, or a reduction on part:340011
trades.why: It says only multi-year volume agreements move prices.

trades.give: volume_per_year commitment plus a rolling forecast
trades.get: Allocation share that covers our growth, plus a firm lead_time_days of 35
trades.why: Allocation is based on last year's call-offs, but our spend keeps rising, so a forecast secures supply.

trades.give: payment_days: commit to paying on time at 30 net
trades.get: Price hold, or any increase capped well below 2 %
trades.why: This costs us almost nothing; we currently pay about 2.9 days late on average, 87 % of the time.

trades.give: volume share kept at today's quota (60 % / 50 %) rather than shifted to the second source
trades.get: ppm_commitment ≤ 300 and an OTD improvement plan toward 95 %
trades.why: OTD and ppm are deteriorating against contract targets.

arguments.point: Clause 3.1 requires written notice of price changes at least 90 days before year-end, i.e. by about 2 Oct 2026. Without timely notice, 2027 prices stay as they are.
OTD is 75.5 % (confirmed 79.2 %) against the 95 % contract target and has declined for three quarters. An increase is hard to justify while it is underdelivering.
ppm rose from 322 to 387, with 11 complaints in 12 months and 2 open 8D reports.
Our spend with it has grown every year (220k → 264k → 288k EUR). We are a growing customer worth a multi-year deal.
Both parts have a qualified second source, so we can shift quota if supply or price is unsatisfactory.

avoid: Demanding a straight discount on standard items; it has explicitly refused this.
Leaning hard on the should-cost gap (+8.1 %). The estimate has only 5 % confidence and an 8 % margin is normal.
Asking for an index clause. Material is only about 4.86 of 34.74 EUR per unit, so it offers little benefit.
Threatening a volume cut during allocation. It may simply allocate less to us.
Asking for anything above 2 % in a single round; it triggers the committee and costs about two weeks.
tone: Factual and partnership-oriented. Frame every request as part of a multi-year volume package, and cite contract clauses and scorecard figures precisely.
red_flags: Allocation based on last year's call-offs may not cover our rising demand on part:340011.
OTD is falling (75.5 %) and ppm is rising (387) with 2 open 8D reports.
A 2027 increase notice may arrive right before the clause 3.1 deadline (about 2 Oct).
We matter little to it (0.8 % of its turnover), so it has little reason to prioritise us under allocation.

evidence.claim: Deliveries of standard mechanical seals are being allocated based on last year's call-offs.
Standard items are not discounted; only multi-year volume agreements change prices.
Price changes above 2 % need pricing committee approval; the committee meets every two weeks.
OTD fell from 80.4 % to 75.5 % and ppm rose from 322 to 387, against a 95 % OTD target.
Prices are fixed per calendar year; changes require 90 days' notice before year-end.
Largest settlements were 2.1 % and 1.8 %; four of six renewals settled at 0 %.
Part:340011 price is 37.55 EUR vs a no-margin should-cost of 34.74 EUR (+8.1 %, low confidence).
Framework runs to 2027-06-30 and auto-extends by 12 months unless terminated with 90 days' notice.

indicators.credit_index: 147 (12 months ago 147; higher is worse, >300 weak)
price_vs_should_cost_no_margin: part:340011: price 37.55 vs cost:340011 34.74 (its own plant): +8.1 %
indicators.scorecard_trend: 2025Q4 green (otd 80.4, ppm 360) → 2026Q1 green (otd 80.4, ppm 322) → 2026Q2 green (otd 76.0, ppm 378) → 2026Q3 green (otd 75.5, ppm 387)
